46:- **Across tracks.** Each clip keeps its place in the stack, counted back from the front. A clip copied from the front track lands on the front track, and one copied from the second track down lands on the second track down. A selection across two lanes pastes back onto two lanes.
47:- **Missing tracks.** If the project has too few tracks, new ones are added at the back.
51:A paste isn't turned down for lack of room. A clip that would break the overlap rule on its track goes on a new track at the front, so it stays visible over what was already there.
53:A smaller overlap is allowed, as it is for any placement: up to half of the shorter clip. The clip stays on its track and the overlap gets a Cross Dissolve. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).
69:Cut follows the same split. Cutting a picture takes its sound with it, unless the sound is on a locked track. Cutting a detached sound on its own leaves the picture in place, silent.
86:- Room for a paste isn't unlimited: a project holds up to 64 tracks and 4,096 clips. A paste that would pass either limit shows an error.
87:- Copy and Paste work inside a nest. **Copy** takes the clips you picked and counts their depth against the nest's own tracks, and **Paste** lands in the nest that's open.
91:`paste` takes a description of the clips in the same form Copy writes, so an agent can place clips without touching your clipboard, at any time and on any track. See [Tools: copy and nest](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/).

29:<kbd>⇧</kbd>-click a clip to add it to the selection. <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click a selected clip to take it out.
33:Drag from any empty part of the timeline: a gap in a lane, the strip under the ruler, or the space below the last lane. A band follows the pointer and selects every clip it touches, however little of the clip it covers.
36:- <kbd>⇧</kbd>-drag adds to the selection. Clips already selected stay selected.
49:**Edit ▸ Select All** (<kbd>⌘A</kbd>) selects every clip in the timeline you're editing, on locked tracks too. With a nest open, it selects the clips inside the nest.
55:**Edit ▸ Select After Playhead** (<kbd>⌥⌘A</kbd>) selects every clip whose start is at or after the playhead, on every track, including locked ones. A clip the playhead is partway through isn't included.
61:<kbd>⌥</kbd>-click a track's header to select every clip on that track, locked or not. On an empty track, this leaves nothing selected.
63:**Edit ▸ Select All on Track** does the same for the current track, which is the track of a selected clip, or the front track when nothing is selected. It's dimmed when the timeline has no clips, and it beeps when the current track is empty.

content.content:
**One microphone for everyone.** When the selection holds exactly one
microphone and two or more cameras, Switch by Speaker decides who talks from
the cameras' pictures instead: while the microphone hears speech, the camera
whose person's mouth moves most is shown — the largest face in each camera,
its mouth opening and closing over half a second, at least half as much again
as the next camera's — and when two mouths move alike it is crosstalk. It
reads Frame Job's on-device face analysis of each camera; when a camera's
faces have not been found yet, an **Analyzing** sheet finds them first (Stop
leaves everything as it was, and what was found is kept), then the Switch by
Speaker sheet opens. That sheet has one **Microphone** pop-up and lists the
**Cameras**; there is no Ignore bleed row, and **Minimum shot** opens at 3 s
and is not remembered. Choose a **Wide** to show it during crosstalk: the wide
camera then takes no part in deciding who talks. The summary starts "Faces
guess who is talking; check the cuts." — mouths that move without speaking
(laughing, chewing, a hand over the mouth) or a face turned away can put a
cut in the wrong place, so look through the result and fix shots with Switch
Angle.

**A limit, measured.** With heavy bleed in a noisy room (another voice 24 dB
down under −45 dBFS of noise), a cut can come later than Cut before speech
asks — in the worst case measured, about 35 ms before the first word instead
of 0.2 s.

## Switch Angle

fixed.now: The paste step says a copy can't sit on top of its original, so it lands on a new track in front of the others, and that track is the program. Added a note that New Track isn't needed and a track added first stays empty behind the copy. Dropped New Track and ⇧⌘N from AtAGlance; both stay in the prose.

fixed.was: Step 3: 'Repeat for each cut.'

fixed.was: 'A camera track that holds anything outside the range isn't hidden.'
fixed.now: '…holds anything outside the range, or any clip without a picture, isn't hidden.'

fixed.was: Still-being-analysed row: 'which often happens straight after an import' (a frequency the code can't settle).
fixed.now: 'which can happen straight after an import'.
fixed.evidence: app/Sources/MediaImporter.swift:209-212 (the cache pass runs after import); app/Sources/SpeakerSwitch+Read.swift:82-89

fixed.was: Late cuts: 'With another voice 24 dB down under −45 dBFS of noise, the worst case measured was about 35 ms before the first word instead of 0.2 s.'
fixed.now: Replaced the measurement with the mechanism: a cut is timed from where a voice first rises above its bleed line and the quiet background, so it can land later than Cut asks. The heading and anchor are unchanged.

fixed.was: 'When two mouths move alike it's crosstalk'.
fixed.now: 'When two mouths move alike, or the busiest mouth stays under that floor, it's crosstalk'.

fixed.now: 'what was saved so far is kept. Frame Job saves as it goes, every 30 seconds.' A stopped job doesn't flush its unpublished samples.

fixed.was: Agent: 'then stops with what it found kept'.
fixed.now: 'then stops, keeping what was saved so far'.
